items.title: Here are the stocks taking a hit amid the Muse hype
items.summary: The 8:30 Hosts Julie Hyman, Jake Conley, and Pras Subramanian look at the stocks taking a hit as Meta's (META) new AI agent, Muse, grows in popularity and why its hype may not measure up to its disruptive potential.

items.title: Meta's Muse AI teams up with Shopify, lifting its stock
items.summary: Meta Platforms' (META) new AI agent Muse is teaming up with Shopify (SHOP) to help and enable consumers to complete online purchases. Yahoo Finance Tech Editor Dan Howley breaks down the value this represents for Meta.

items.title: Anthropic vs. OpenAI: Competition heats up with release of new AI models
items.summary: Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) unveiled its new Claude Opus 5.5 on Tuesday, the developer's latest AI model promising faster performance and lower costs for enterprise customers. Yahoo Finance Tech Editor Dan Howley examines the tightening AI competition between Anthropic and OpenAI (OPAI.PVT), which also just released its new GPT-6 Sol and Luna models.

items.title: WBD Stock Is Running. Is There Fuel Left?
items.summary: After a powerful run to new highs, this media giant's stock is asking every investor the same question: is the turnaround in streaming enough to carry the whole company higher.

items.title: Shopify Sinks 5%, Meta Ticks Up as Muse Deal Rally Unwinds; Amazon Slips
items.summary: Two partners in the same agentic checkout deal are moving in opposite directions Wednesday morning, and a fresh move by one of the world's largest storefronts is rewriting the ceiling on how far the agreement can reach.

items.title: Is Snowflake Buying Its Growth With Its Margin?
items.summary: Snowflake (SNOW) stock has gained about 50% since late December 2025, against 13% for the S&P 500. Microsoft, Amazon, and Alphabet all trailed the index over the same stretch. So this was not the cloud trade lifting everything at once. One number inside Snowflake moved, and management has already said what it costs to keep it moving.

items.title: What Microsoft's Trailing Multiple Leaves Out
items.summary: Microsoft (MSFT) has returned about 33% over the past three months, though it is down 3.1% over the past twelve months. Near $500 a share, the stock carries a trailing price-to-earnings ratio of about 26.7 times adjusted earnings. Whether that multiple looks elevated or not, it is the wrong number to make the decision on, because the earnings analysts already expect are not in it.
